page: Amazon Web Services m7i.large is an entry-level general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and a custom fourth-generation Intel Xeon Scalable processor (model 8488C). Based on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical execution core with two hyper-threads operating at 3.2 GHz. The instance configuration includes 8.0 GB of DDR5 system memory running at 5 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). The underlying processor features 105 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware acceleration extensions including Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) and AVX-512.

Hardware configurations on the m7i.large exclude integrated local instance storage, requiring workloads to rely on remote block storage solutions. Network connectivity features a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are allocated by default. Graphics acceleration is absent, with zero bundled GPUs. In synthetic benchmarks, single-threaded throughput shows stable average performance, achieving 1845.29 in stress-ng and 1747.0 in Geekbench single-core evaluations. Gzip compression achieves 28.02 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaches 11.78 GB/sec.

Because the instance supplies only a single physical core, multi-threaded capacity reflects predictable scaling limitations. Multi-core evaluations show 1895.08 in stress-ng and 2133.0 in Geekbench, both placing in lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth throughput registers at 13.5 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 14.89 GB/sec for writes. Workload tests show 2.6 million Redis SET operations per second and 4.18 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The instance delivers a balanced resource allocation profile suited for predictable, low-concurrency tasks. It is best applied to standard web serving, microservices, continuous integration build nodes, small staging environments, and intermediate caching layers that do not demand extensive multi-threaded execution or high local input-output capacity.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i.large is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and built on the AWS Nitro system. Powered by a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon Scalable 8488C processor, it features 2 vCPUs provisioned across 1 physical core with 2 threads, paired with 8.0 GB of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5 memory. The instance includes advanced instruction sets like Intel AMX and AVX-512, but does not provide onboard local storage or dedicated GPU acceleration. Network connectivity operates at a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Benchmark testing indicates mid-tier single-threaded compute capability alongside modest multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth, which reflects its dual-vCPU footprint. The m7i.large is technically positioned for lightweight general-purpose applications, microservices, small API backends, static web serving, and development environments requiring consistent processor performance without intensive parallel processing demands.
